Term definitions and diagrams you can cite. Week notes link here on **first use**. Cards use a short lecture pattern (**what → why in LAE → watch-out**) where it helps. Source type is shown by **section** (Hong Kong law, Mainland comparator, course economics, …) — not by a per-term Official/Course tag. Large projections (e.g. HK$350bn) are attributed on [Official status](tracker.qmd) and [Key figures](key-figures.qmd).

## At a glance

Captions list sources; entries start at [Hong Kong institutions and law](#hong-kong-institutions-and-law); also [Mainland comparators](#mainland-comparators) and [EU / US comparators](#eu-us-comparators).

Sources (as of 6 Oct 2026): Working Group led by the Deputy Financial Secretary ([2024 Policy Address ¶82](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2024/en/p81.html)); Secretary for Transport and Logistics as Deputy Head, and TLB carrying out Sandbox pilot projects by batches ([GIA, 12 Nov 2024](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202411/12/P2024111200260.htm)); Working Group selection of Sandbox projects ([GIA, 20 Mar 2025](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202503/20/P2025032000179.htm)) and Sandbox X projects ([TLB](https://www.tlb.gov.hk/eng/highlights/transport/low-altitude.html)); Sandbox X launch ([GIA, 24 Nov 2025](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202511/24/P2025112400912.htm)); Action Plan still being formulated ([STL to LegCo, 2 Oct 2026, Chinese only](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/02/P2026100200677.htm); [2026 Policy Address ¶139](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/en/chapter3.html)); TLB indicators 34–35 ([PA Annex](https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202609/16/P2026091600270_557059_1_1789541487116.pdf)); CAD technical study on the traffic management system, and Sandbox X cross-boundary trial flights “as soon as practicable” ([TLB LegCo reply, 24 Jun 2026](https://www.tlb.gov.hk/eng/legislative/transport/replies/2026/20260624a.html)); CAD as Cap. 448G regulator ([CAD](https://www.cad.gov.hk/english/sua.html); [Cap. 448G](https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap448G)); [G.N. 5936](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.5936_E.pdf); [AC-013](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_E.pdf); [AC-017](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-017.pdf); 1.4 GHz licence, CAD flight-path approval and Sandbox-only use ([OFCA](https://www.ofca.gov.hk/en/industry_focus/industry_focus/uas_private_licence/index.html)); Civil Aviation Law and Art. 258 ([CAAC](https://www.caac.gov.cn/XXGK/XXGK/FLFG/202512/t20251227_229597.html); [CAAC English](https://www.caac.gov.cn/English/News/202512/t20251230_229616.html)); [国令761](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202306/content_6888800.htm); CCAR-92 and §92.5 ([Ministry of Transport](https://xxgk.mot.gov.cn/2020/jigou/fgs/202401/t20240103_3980642.html)); ATM Rules draft ([CAAC](https://www.caac.gov.cn/HDJL/YJZJ/202608/t20260811_231462.html)); 粤府办〔2024〕6号 and its Greater Bay Area corridor aim ([Guangdong](https://www.gd.gov.cn/gkmlpt/content/4/4427/post_4427812.html)).

Dashed boxes and dashed arrows (OPEN, PLANNED, DRAFT) are not yet established. Solid arrows are relationships stated in the sources above. Corridor and Sandbox status: [Official status](tracker.qmd).

### Altitude scale

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 30, "rankSpacing": 26, "padding": 10, "wrappingWidth": 520}}}%%
flowchart BT
    G0["Ground level (真高 0)"]
    A1["<b>Hong Kong</b> · 100 ft above ground level (≈ 30 m)<br/>maximum flying altitude, Category A1"]
    A2["<b>Hong Kong</b> · 300 ft above ground level (≈ 91 m)<br/>maximum flying altitude, Category A2<br/>and exempted Category A1 models<br/>higher only with CAD permission (Cap. 448G s.37)"]
    M120["<b>Mainland</b> · 真高120米<br/>国令761 Art. 19: above 真高120米 = UAS 管制空域<br/>W类空域 = part of G类空域 below 真高120米<br/>(微型 / 轻型 / 小型 UAS)"]
    M300["<b>Mainland</b> · 真高300米<br/>G类空域 includes airspace below 真高300米<br/>outside B / C classes (W excluded)<br/>国令761 Art. 22: 小型 UAS 融合飞行<br/>up to 真高300米 needs ATM approval"]
    K1000["<b>Hong Kong</b> · about 1,000 m<br/>LAE = economic activities in airspace<br/>“generally below 1 000 metres”<br/>policy description, not a flying limit"]
    G0 --- A1 --- A2 --- M120 --- M300 --- K1000
    classDef hk fill:#f4f7fb,stroke:#003366,color:#1a1a1a
    classDef cn fill:#f8f6f1,stroke:#7a6a4f,color:#1a1a1a

    class A1,A2 hk
    class M120,M300 cn
    class K1000 pol
    class G0 gnd
```

Sources (as of 6 Oct 2026): Category A1 100 ft and Category A2 300 ft above ground level, specified under Cap. 448G s.17(2) for s.16(1)(c) ([G.N. 1276 of 2022](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.1276_E.pdf); [Chinese](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.1276_C.pdf); [SRD §7.4.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/Safety_Requirements_Document.pdf); [AC-013 §6.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_E.pdf)); exempted Category A1 models flown to the Category A2 operating requirements ([G.N. 2303 of 2022](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.2303_E.pdf)); permission under s.37 ([Cap. 448G](https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap448G)); LAE as economic activities in airspace “generally below 1 000 metres” ([LegCo CB(3)933/2024](https://www.legco.gov.hk/yr2024/english/panels/edev/papers/edev20241203cb3-933-3-e.pdf); [2024 Policy Address ¶81](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2024/en/p81.html)); 真高120米 管制空域 (Art. 19) and 真高300米 融合飞行 (Art. 22) ([国令761](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202306/content_6888800.htm)); G类 and W类空域 ([国家空域基础分类方法, CAAC](https://www.caac.gov.cn/XXGK/XXGK/TZTG/202312/t20231221_222397.html)).

Boxes are in height order but not to scale; Hong Kong metre figures are conversions (1 ft = 0.3048 m). The Mainland classification excludes the Hong Kong flight information region, so its labels are not Hong Kong law.

Sources (as of 6 Oct 2026): weight thresholds (s.3(2)), the 150 kg SUA ceiling (s.3(1)), s.10, s.11(1)(a)–(g) and s.37 ([Cap. 448G](https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap448G); [Chinese](https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap448G!zh-Hant-HK.pdf)); Category C from 18 July 2025 ([GIA, 17 Jul 2025](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202507/17/P2025071700590.htm)); rating types and the minimum age of 18 for Advanced Rating (C) ([SRD §5.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/Safety_Requirements_Document.pdf)); Cap. 448C provisions for trial operations of unconventional aircraft “under specified conditions” ([TLB LegCo reply, 24 Jun 2026](https://www.tlb.gov.hk/eng/legislative/transport/replies/2026/20260624a.html)); drafting to be completed within 2027 ([2026 Policy Address Annex, indicator 35](https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202609/16/P2026091600270_557059_1_1789541487116.pdf); [2026 Policy Address ¶139](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/en/chapter3.html)).

Each step adds to the ones on its left. A Category A1 flight that does not meet the s.10 conditions falls under the s.11 basic requirements. Any flight beyond the operating requirements, within a restricted flying zone or carrying dangerous goods needs a s.37 permission ([SRD §8.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/Safety_Requirements_Document.pdf)). Insurance (s.11(1)(c), s.12) is left out: CAD lists its effective date for standard operations as “to be determined” ([CAD](https://www.cad.gov.hk/english/sua_overview_regulatoryreq.html)). The over-150 kg legislation is PLANNED.

Sources (as of 6 Oct 2026): VLOS with a visual observer at the same location ([G.N. 1276 of 2022 ¶(2)](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.1276_E.pdf); [AC-013 §2.6.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_E.pdf)); EVLOS with a visual observer at a different location, not routinely permitted, s.37 permission and Advanced Rating ([AC-004 §1.2–1.3, §2.3–2.4, §5.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-004_E.pdf); [SRD §7.3](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/Safety_Requirements_Document.pdf)); BVLOS definition, Regulatory Sandbox applications, operator experience options and Advanced Rating ([AC-013 §2.6.2, §3.2, §4.2(a), §8.1](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_E.pdf)); standard and advanced operations, rating types and the Advanced Operations Permission ([SRD §5.1.1, §8.1–8.3](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/Safety_Requirements_Document.pdf)); Chinese terms ([AC-013 Chinese §2.6](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_C.pdf); [AC-004 Chinese](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-004_C.pdf)).

The mapping is not one-to-one: a VLOS flight still needs permission and an Advanced Rating when it is an advanced operation, and the Advanced Operations Permission is one of two experience routes for a BVLOS operator, not a required step (AC-013 also says an operator without BVLOS experience may still be considered). This diagram covers BVLOS in the Regulatory Sandbox only; Sandbox X cross-boundary flights are under AC-017.

UAV, VTOL and eVTOL are industry usage, as in their entries below.

No arrow joins the two groups: LAE and 低空经济 measure economic activity and are not aircraft categories. The dedicated unconventional-aircraft legislation is PLANNED.

### Terms that must not be mixed

HK **1,000 m** working definition ≠ Mainland airspace **120 m / 300 m** class labels.

## Hong Kong institutions and law
**Action Plan on Developing Low-Altitude Economy (發展低空經濟規劃行動綱領)**  

**What:** 2025 PA ¶154; text OPEN.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="官方中英文本 · Official English and Chinese"}
English: “We will formulate the Action Plan on Developing Low-Altitude Economy to advance Hong Kong as a major hub for low-altitude applications through institutional innovations and technological breakthroughs.” ([source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2025/en/p153.html))

[「我們會制訂「發展低空經濟規劃行動綱領」，透過制度創新與技術突破，令香港成為低空創新應用的核心樞紐」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2025/tc/p153.html))
:::


**advanced operations (進階操作)**  

**What:** SUA operations that require prior CAD permission under Cap. 448G (as distinct from ordinary permitted flying). Cap. 448G / CAD.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**[Regulatory Sandbox (監管沙盒)]{#regulatory-sandbox}**

**What:** Hong Kong’s earlier controlled trial programme for selected LAE applications under approved conditions. Applications from 13 November 2024; **38 of 72** proposals selected (TLB/GIA, 20 March 2025). BVLOS in this programme is covered by CAD AC-013.

**Why in LAE:** Lets firms and agencies learn before full-scale deployment — an economic response to high entry barriers.

**Watch-out:** First-batch selection **38 of 72** is **not** the same as later Sandbox X module counts. A sandbox does **not** waive safety. See [Key figures](key-figures.qmd).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="官方中英文本 · Official English and Chinese"}
English: “The Government received Regulatory Sandbox pilot project proposals from 72 applicants, and after review by the Working Group on Developing LAE, 38 of them are among the first batch of pilot projects to be rolled out” ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202503/20/P2025032000179.htm))

[「政府共接獲由72個申請者提交的「監管沙盒」試點項目申請，經發展低空經濟工作組審閱後，其中38項成為首批推展的試點項目」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202503/20/P2025032000178.htm))
:::

**[Regulatory Sandbox X (監管沙盒 X / 監管沙盒X)]{#sandbox-x}**

**What:** A **later, separate** Hong Kong trial programme launched 24 November 2025 (modules such as UTM, unconventional aircraft, shared platforms). CAD AC-017 covers cross-boundary operations in Sandbox X.

**Why in LAE:** Cross-boundary and advanced modules appear here — still trials, not day-to-day corridor service.

**Watch-out:** **Sandbox X ≠ the first Regulatory Sandbox.** Do not add 38 and 33 into one “market share.” See [Key figures](key-figures.qmd); [Who decides what?](regulators.qmd#standing-caveats).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="官方中英文本 · Official English and Chinese"}
English: “The launch event of the low-altitude economy \"Regulatory Sandbox X\" was held today (November 24), with an aim to further promoting the development of low-altitude economy in Hong Kong and exploring innovative applications.” ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202511/24/P2025112400912.htm))

[「低空經濟「監管沙盒X」啟動禮今日（十一月二十四日）舉行，旨在進一步推動香港的低空經濟發展，並探索創新應用場景。」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202511/24/P2025112400779.htm))

English: “(i) 15 pilot projects under the UTM system demonstrations module, (ii) a first batch of four pilot projects under the unconventional aircraft module; (iii) a first batch of five pilot projects under the multiple applications/users shared-platform module; and (iv) a first batch of nine pilot projects under the others module have been selected for implementation in phases.” ([source](https://www.tlb.gov.hk/eng/highlights/transport/low-altitude.html))

[「經發展低空經濟工作組審閱後，已選定(i) 15個UTM系統演示試點項目；(ii) 首批四個非傳統航空器試點項目；(iii) 首批五個多場景／多用戶共享平台試點項目，以及(iv) 首批九個其他試點項目予以分階段推行。」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.tlb.gov.hk/tc/highlights/transport/low-altitude.html))

## EU / US comparators

Course comparators only — **not Hong Kong law**. Dated instruments on [Timeline](dates.qmd); documents on the week pages under **Teach**.

**AiRMOUR**  

**What:** EU Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Action (grant **101006601**; **1 Jan 2021** → **31 Dec 2023**) that researched and validated urban air mobility concepts for emergency medical services; coordinated by VTT (Finland); **project closed**. **Not** a company, aircraft brand, or OEM product name (CORDIS lists participants separately). Course comparator — not Hong Kong law. See also Course overview; Lectures (Week 4); EASA. [CORDIS](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101006601); [airmour.eu](https://airmour.eu/project-description/).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**EASA (European Union Aviation Safety Agency)**  

**What:** EU aviation safety agency used as a **course comparator**. Site evidence: SC-VTOL-01 Issue 1 (2 Jul 2019) as the airworthiness special condition for small VTOL-capable aircraft; ED Decision 2025/011/R (7 Jul 2025) adding crew and operations material for innovative air mobility / manned VTOL-capable aircraft; prototype vertiport design specifications and a societal-acceptance study on Readings. U-space itself is created by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/664 (Timeline) — an EU framework, not an EASA-only instrument; later EASA rows are technical conditions, not a new U-space regulation. See also U-space; Vertiport; eVTOL; Timeline (European Union); Readings. Timeline / Readings / Course overview.

**Why in LAE:** Course and Orient pages point here so law, comparator, and industry labels stay distinct.

**Watch-out:** Comparator or industry labels are **not** automatically Hong Kong law.

**FAA (Federal Aviation Administration)**  

**What:** US aviation authority used as a **course comparator**. Site evidence: Remote ID final rule (Federal Register publication 15 Jan 2021); UAM Concept of Operations v2.0 (26 Apr 2023); UTM Concept of Operations and AAM Implementation Plan on Readings; Integration of Powered-Lift final rule (powered-lift is the FAA category closest to many eVTOL designs). Do **not** confuse the US Remote ID rule with this Glossary’s **Remote ID** entry (CAD AC-017 §8.2). See also UTM; eVTOL; Timeline (United States); Readings. Timeline / Readings / Course overview.

**Why in LAE:** Course and Orient pages point here so law, comparator, and industry labels stay distinct.

**Watch-out:** Comparator or industry labels are **not** automatically Hong Kong law.

## Vehicles and operations
**300 ft AGL operating limit (飛行高度不高於地面以上 300 呎)**  

**What:** Maximum flying altitude for Category A2 SUA (and exempted Category A1 models flown to Category A2 requirements): 300 ft above ground level; Category A1's limit is 100 ft. Higher only with CAD permission under Cap. 448G s.37. G.N. 1276 of 2022; SRD §7.4.1; CAD AC-013 §6.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Air risk (空中風險)**  

**What:** Risk of collision or conflict with other airspace users during the SUA flight. CAD AC-013 §4.3(f).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Automatic operation (自動操作)**  

**What:** SUA follows pre-determined routes, but the remote pilot must still be able to intervene for unforeseen events. CAD AC-013 §2.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Autonomous operation (自主操作)**  

**What:** SUA flies without the remote pilot being able to intervene; **not allowed** for Sandbox BVLOS under AC-013. CAD AC-013 §2.2, §6.7.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**[BVLOS (超視距操作)]{#bvlos}**

**What:** **Beyond visual line of sight** — flying when the remote pilot cannot see the aircraft with their own eyes.

**Why in LAE:** Many useful logistics and inspection missions need BVLOS; it sits behind a higher permission bar than simple VLOS.

**Watch-out:** Do not merge AC-013 (BVLOS in the first Regulatory Sandbox) with AC-017 (Sandbox X cross-boundary). Keep **Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X**. See [Week 7](week-07.qmd).

**C2 link (指揮和與控制數據鏈路)**  

**What:** Command-and-control communications link between the remote pilot / ground systems and the SUA. CAD AC-013 §5.5; AC-017 §5.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Category A1 / A2 / B / C (甲一類 / 甲二類 / 乙類 / 丙類)**  

**What:** Weight-based SUA classes under Cap. 448G; Category C covers above 25 kg up to 150 kg (from 2025-07-18). Cap. 448G s.2, s.3(2) (Cat C expansion 2025-07-18).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

English: “The amendments to the Small Unmanned Aircraft (SUA) Order (Cap. 448G) serve to extend the existing regulatory regime to cover SUA weighing over 25 kilograms but not exceeding 150kg.”…“The Small Unmanned Aircraft (Amendment) Order 2025 and the Air Navigation (Hong Kong) Order 1995 (Amendment) Order 2025 will come into effect tomorrow (July 18) to facilitate the development of the low-altitude economy.” ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202507/17/P2025071700590.htm))

[「修訂《小型無人機令》（第448G章）旨在擴闊現行規管制度，以涵蓋重量超過25公斤但不超過150公斤的小型無人機。」…「《2025年小型無人機（修訂）令》和《2025年〈1995年飛航（香港）令〉（修訂）令》，將於明日（七月十八日）生效，以推動低空經濟的發展。」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202507/17/P2025071700589.htm))
:::


**Congested area (人口稠密區域 / 人口密集區域)**  

**What:** Built-up area where BVLOS routes that raise ground risk should normally be avoided unless justified to CAD. CAD AC-013 §5.2; Cap. 448G operating context.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Containment**  

**What:** Keeping the SUA entirely inside the pre-defined sandbox operating areas or routes by technology and/or procedures. CAD AC-013 §4.3(d), §5.3.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Cross-boundary SUA operation (跨境小型無人機操作 / 跨境操作)**  

**What:** SUA flight that is **not** wholly within Hong Kong; Cap. 448G treats it as an advanced operation needing CAD permission — AC-017 covers Sandbox X cross-boundary (no person on board). Cap. 448G s.16(1A); CAD AC-017.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Daylight-only default (只限日間時間操作)**  

**What:** Default operating requirement to fly SUA only in daylight hours unless a relevant permission is obtained. Cap. 448G / SRD; CAD AC-013 §6.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Detect and avoid (探測與避障)**  

**What:** Capability to see, sense or detect conflicting traffic or other hazards and take appropriate action — concept only, no product brand. CAD AC-013 §2.3.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**docking station (無人機機庫)**  

**What:** Ground unit for automated launch, recovery, charging or swapping of small unmanned aircraft; CAD AC-016 addresses hangar/dock-style SUA operations — **not** a vertiport statute. CAD AC-016; industry usage.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

[「使用無人機機庫進行小型無人機操作的指引及許可」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-016_C.pdf))
:::


**EVLOS (延伸視線操作)**  

**What:** Operation beyond simple VLOS but still using visual observers or procedures — not BVLOS. CAD / Cap. 448G practice.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**[eVTOL (電動垂直起降飛行器)]{#evtol}**

**What:** Industry label for **electric vertical take-off and landing** craft (take off and land roughly straight up and down, usually with electric power).

**Why in LAE:** Passenger and some cargo concepts in slides are often eVTOL-shaped — few seats, high fixed cost per passenger unless utilization is high.

**Watch-out:** Hong Kong has **no dedicated eVTOL statute yet**. Treat eVTOL as a technology concept under discussion, not a finished local licensing category. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="官方中英文本 · Official English and Chinese"}
English: “Improve civil aviation legislation and regulatory framework, including formulating dedicated legislation for unconventional aircraft weighing over 150 kilograms, to lay the foundation for developing the standardisation of the low-altitude economy.” ([source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2025/en/p153.html))

[「完善民航法例及規管框架，為重量超過150公斤的「非傳統飛行器」制訂專用法例，為低空經濟標準化發展奠下基礎。」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2025/tc/p153.html))
:::

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Flyaway (飛失)**  

**What:** Official Chinese form 飛失. CAD AC-013_C §14.1(f).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**What:** SUA safety-system function that supports awareness of geographical limits; required with flight log under Cap. 448G s.13 / AC-013. Cap. 448G s.13; CAD AC-013 §10.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**What:** Electronic or procedural boundary that keeps the SUA inside pre-defined sandbox operating areas or flight routes. CAD AC-013 §5.3, App. A §3.6.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**What:** Maximum certified take-off weight; Cap. 448G categories and Mainland UAS rules key off weight thresholds. Cap. 448G; Mainland UAS instruments.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**payload (載荷)**

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Remote ID**  

**What:** Continuous broadcast of SUA identity and geographic position so aircraft in the air can be identified. CAD AC-017 §8.2.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Remote pilot (遙控駕駛員)**  

**What:** Person who manipulates the flight controls of a SUA during flight under Cap. 448G. Cap. 448G; CAD AC-013 §7.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Return-to-home (自動返航 / 返航點)**  

**What:** Pre-programmed recovery behaviour that sends the SUA to a home or safe site (e.g. after C2-link loss); incorrect RTH settings are a containment hazard. CAD AC-013 §14.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Specific Operations Risk Assessment (SORA) (特定運行風險評估)**  

**What:** Official Chinese form 特定運行風險評估. CAD AC-013_C App. B (names SORA).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**[SUA (小型無人機)]{#sua}**

**What:** **Small unmanned aircraft** — Hong Kong Cap. 448G’s main legal label for unmanned aircraft **not more than 150 kg**, with weight classes A1 → C.

**Why in LAE:** Almost every “drone” discussion in this course must be checked against SUA rules (and whether the craft is above the SUA ceiling).

**Watch-out:** Everyday “drone” is **not** a Cap. 448G synonym. Heavier / passenger concepts may sit as **unconventional aircraft** pending rules. See [Key figures](key-figures.qmd); [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**Surveillance system (監察系統)**  

**What:** Means (or alternative compliance) for the remote pilot to monitor the SUA and nearby traffic/obstacles during higher-risk BVLOS. CAD AC-013 §10.9.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**UAS**  

**What:** Unmanned aircraft system (aircraft + control station + links); used in OFCA licence titles and Mainland instruments; broader than Cap. 448G “SUA.”. OFCA UAS (Private) Licence; Mainland 国令761 / CCAR-92 usage.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**UAV**  

**What:** Common label for the aircraft alone; prefer **SUA** when citing Cap. 448G and **UAS** when citing system or spectrum rules. Course / industry usage.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Uninvolved person (非參與人員)**  

**What:** Any person other than an involved person; drives ground-risk planning for BVLOS. CAD AC-013 §2.5.2.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**Visual observer (視像觀察員)**  

**What:** Person at the same location as the remote pilot who keeps unaided visual contact with the SUA and communicates to help avoid collision. CAD AC-013 §2.6.1; official Chinese form 視像觀察員 in [G.N. 1276 ¶(2)](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/G.N.1276_C.pdf) and CAD AC-013_C §2.6.1.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**[VLOS (視線內操作)]{#vlos}**

**What:** **Visual line of sight** — the remote pilot (or required observers, when rules say so) can see the aircraft during the flight.

**Why in LAE:** Baseline for simpler SUA operations; BVLOS is the step beyond.

**Watch-out:** VLOS is not the same as “we have cameras on board.” Legal VLOS is about human visual contact under Cap. 448G / ACs as applicable.

**VTOL**  

**What:** Vertical take-off and landing as a flight capability, whether electric or not; broader than eVTOL. Course / industry usage.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**What:** Official Chinese form 禁區／限制區／危險區. CAD AC-013_C §5.1(b).

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**Watch-out:** Do not treat a slide shorthand as a substitute for the legal or issuer definition. When unsure, check [Official status](tracker.qmd) or the linked week.

**restricted flying zone (限制飛行區)**  

**What:** CAD-designated area where SUA flight is restricted or needs permission; cite current CAD maps/notices, not press maps. CAD; official Chinese form 限制飛行區 in Cap. 448G s.2.

**What:** Policy-Address label for the planned digital traffic-management layer of low-altitude infrastructure; Hong Kong system still **planned**, not a statute. 2024 PA LAE infra slide; 2025 PA ¶154.

**Why in LAE:** You will meet this name in readings, permissions, or week notes — keep the issuer wording exact.

**[U-space]{#u-space}**

**What:** An EU / industry framework for managing unmanned traffic in designated airspace volumes.

**Why in LAE:** Useful comparator when readings talk about digital traffic services and roles.

**Watch-out:** **U-space is not Hong Kong law.** Do not cite it as a local compliance pathway. See [Who decides what?](regulators.qmd).

**[UTM]{#utm}**

**What:** **Unmanned aircraft system traffic management** — industry language for digital services that help plan, authorize, and monitor unmanned flights.

**Why in LAE:** Coordination cost and shared information show up in Weeks 7–8 and in Sandbox X UTM modules.

**Watch-out:** Hong Kong’s Smart Low-altitude Traffic Management System is **planned** (Policy Address language: progressive implementation from **2028**) — not a claim that city-wide UTM already exists. **U-space ≠ Hong Kong law.** See [Key figures](key-figures.qmd).

**[Throughput]{#throughput}**

**What:** How many movements, passengers, or missions a facility can process in a period.

**Why in LAE:** Breakeven capacity use and slot design need a throughput number, not only a pretty site map.

**Watch-out:** Design capacity is not the same as reliable throughput after weather and acceptance limits. See [Week 5](week-05.qmd).

**[Vertiport (起降場)]{#vertiport}**

**What:** Industry word for a take-off and landing site for advanced craft (plus related ground handling).

**Why in LAE:** Site cost, throughput, and slots often bind before aircraft do (Week 5).

**Watch-out:** Hong Kong has **no dedicated vertiport statute yet**. “Vertiport” in class is a managerial label, not an official local classification. See [Week 5](week-05.qmd).

## Business and economics

Course economics vocabulary in plain English. Each card: **what it is** → **why it matters in LAE** → **watch-out**. Law and programme names live in the sections above — typology is by **section heading**, not a per-term Official/Course tag. Worked numbers stay on **Teach**; citeable programme facts stay on [Key figures](key-figures.qmd) / [Official status](tracker.qmd).

**[AAM]{#aam}**  

**What:** **Advanced air mobility** — a broad industry label for new aircraft concepts that may link cities, suburbs, or corridors.

**Why in LAE:** Readings use AAM as a **comparator** frame next to Hong Kong-first LAE and city **UAM**.

**Watch-out:** AAM language is **not** Hong Kong law. Nesting: LAE (umbrella) ⊃ UAM (in-city) ; AAM is broader industry talk. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[ASK / available capacity unit]{#ask}**  

**What:** Capacity you **offer** (seat-km or payload-km), used as the denominator in CASK / CPMK.

**Why in LAE:** Separates “how much capacity did we put in the sky?” from “how much was used?” (load factor).

**Watch-out:** ASK is not demand and not revenue. Classroom CASK figures are teaching tools, not market data. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[ATC (average total cost)]{#atc-average-total-cost}**  

**What:** **Average total cost** — total cost divided by units of output (flights, missions, or passengers — say which).

**Why in LAE:** Shows how **fixed cost** spreads when utilization or density rises on the same corridor or pad (Weeks 2–3).

**Watch-out:** This is **not** Air Traffic Control (the aviation safety / traffic service). For traffic-control language see [Airspace and traffic](#airspace-and-traffic).

**[availability payment]{#availability-payment}**  

**What:** Payment for **readiness** of a service or asset, even when usage is low.

**Why in LAE:** Public or partner deals often buy “be ready to fly” for emergency or sparse routes, not only pay-per-trip.

**Watch-out:** Availability pay does **not** prove there is commercial demand. Contrast [usage payment](#usage-payment). See [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[Bertrand competition]{#bertrand}**  

**What:** Price competition when rivals set **prices** (rather than quantities).

**Why in LAE:** With scarce pads, undercutting toward marginal cost can destroy margins if average cost stays high.

**Watch-out:** Textbook Bertrand needs a clear product and free capacity. Pad limits change the story. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[Break-even load factor]{#break-even-load-factor}**  

**What:** The load factor at which revenue covers a stated cost block.

**Why in LAE:** Links “how full must we be?” to a cost target before you talk about profit.

**Watch-out:** Only as good as the cost block you chose. See also [breakeven volume](#breakeven-volume); [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[breakeven volume]{#breakeven-volume}**  

**What:** How many flights, passengers, or missions you need to cover fixed cost at a stated contribution per unit.

**Why in LAE:** Turns a cost stack into a volume target you can compare with capacity and demand.

**Watch-out:** Breakeven on a clear-weather day can fail when downtime cuts volume. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[CAPEX / OPEX]{#capex-opex}**  

**What:** **CAPEX** = capital expenditure (upfront investment). **OPEX** = operating expenditure (recurring running costs).

**Why in LAE:** Mixing them hides whether a problem is “too expensive to build” or “too expensive to run every day.”

**Watch-out:** Label the period. Some costs look fixed in a week and variable over a year. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[cash flow]{#cash-flow}**  

**What:** Money in minus money out in a period.

**Why in LAE:** NPV and staging decisions need cash timing, not only accounting profit labels.

**Watch-out:** State what is included (tax, partner fees, CAPEX). See [NPV](#npv).

**[CASK / CPMK]{#cask-cpmk}**  

**What:** **CASK** = cost per available seat-kilometre; **CPMK** = cost per available payload-kilometre — cost of **capacity offered**.

**Why in LAE:** Compares unit cost when seats or payload-km are the natural unit (passenger vs cargo / mission).

**Watch-out:** Lecture CASK numbers are **not** Hong Kong market data. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[contribution margin]{#contribution-margin}**  

**What:** Revenue minus variable cost (before fixed cost).

**Why in LAE:** Shows whether an extra trip helps pay the lease — the heart of revenue management and breakeven.

**Watch-out:** Positive contribution can still lose money after fixed cost. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[co-opetition]{#co-opetition}**  

**What:** Cooperate on shared assets (for example a pad) while competing on service.

**Why in LAE:** Scarce roofs push rivals to share infrastructure without merging brands.

**Watch-out:** Sharing can cut unit cost and harden price competition at the same time. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd) / [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[congestion externality]{#congestion-externality}**  

**What:** Extra delay (and related cost) you impose on others when scarce airspace or pad capacity is used.

**Why in LAE:** Private flight decisions can ignore spillover delay, so queues grow too far.

**Watch-out:** Classroom congestion charges are appraisal aids — not a published Hong Kong drone congestion tax. See [Week 8](week-08.qmd).

**[demand funnel]{#demand-funnel}**  

**What:** A step-down from relevant trips → choice → **served** demand under capacity.

**Why in LAE:** Stops “huge TAM” slides from skipping pads, weather, and acceptance.

**Watch-out:** Unconstrained funnel headlines are not obtainable revenue. See [Week 4](week-04.qmd) / [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[discount rate]{#discount-rate}**  

**What:** The rate used to turn future cash into present value in NPV.

**Why in LAE:** Higher rates punish distant cash — important when certification and sandboxes delay launch.

**Watch-out:** Always state the rate; it is an assumption, not a law of nature. See [NPV](#npv).

**[economies of density]{#economies-of-density}**  

**What:** Average cost falls as more flights share the **same** corridor or vertiport (not only “bigger aircraft”).

**Why in LAE:** Density can look like a moat when sites are scarce.

**Watch-out:** Density needs allowed volume — demand, pads, and rules can bind first. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[elasticity of demand]{#elasticity-of-demand}**  

**What:** How quantity responds to a price change. **Own-price** = your price; **cross-price** = a rival or substitute’s price.

**Why in LAE:** Strong MTR / taxi alternatives can make air fares very sensitive.

**Watch-out:** Elasticity from a survey without alternatives can understate switching. See [Week 4](week-04.qmd).

**[entry barrier]{#entry-barrier}**  

**What:** Cost or delay that slows or blocks new entry (investment, compliance, waiting, uncertainty).

**Why in LAE:** Explains why controlled trials exist — learn before irreversible scale-up.

**Watch-out:** A sandbox may cut **delay** and **uncertainty**; it does **not** waive Cap. 448G or safety duties. Keep **Regulatory Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X**. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd) / [Week 7](week-07.qmd).

**[externality]{#externality}**  

**What:** A cost or benefit that falls on others and is not fully priced into the private ticket or fee (noise, privacy, carbon, risk).

**Why in LAE:** Communities and rules can shrink the operating window even when a fare looks fine.

**Watch-out:** Put externalities in cash flow or capacity limits — not only in an ESG footnote. See [Week 10](week-10.qmd).

**[fixed cost]{#fixed-cost}**  

**What:** A cost that does not change when you add one more flight or passenger in the short run (classroom example: a daily aircraft lease).

**Why in LAE:** The same lease spread over fewer flights means a higher cost per flight or per passenger. Curfews and pad limits that cut daily flights raise fixed cost per flight even if the aircraft is unchanged.

**Watch-out:** “Fixed” depends on the time window. Over a longer horizon, leases and staff can become variable. Always state the period. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[generalised cost]{#generalised-cost}**  

**What:** Money cost plus time valued at the traveller’s **value of time (VOT)**. Also written **generalized cost (GC)**.

**Why in LAE:** Compares air options with MTR, taxi, or Airport Express on one scale — door-to-door, not cruise time only.

**Watch-out:** A GC fare ceiling is not a forecast price. Waiting and access can destroy the time advantage. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd) / [Week 4](week-04.qmd).

**[hedonic valuation]{#hedonic-valuation}**  

**What:** Linking market prices to measurable attributes (for example noise) while controlling for other factors.

**Why in LAE:** Classroom tool for how “quiet” or “view” might show up in prices or discounts.

**Watch-out:** Illustrative coefficients are **not** a Hong Kong drone-noise study. See [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[HHI]{#hhi}**  

**What:** **Herfindahl–Hirschman Index** — sum of squared market shares; a classroom concentration screen.

**Why in LAE:** Summarises how uneven shares look **after** you define product, place, and layer (operator vs site owner).

**Watch-out:** HHI does not prove abuse, does not fix the “pie” metric, and ignores substitutes outside your definition. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[Industry value-added]{#industry-value-added}**  

**What:** An accounting idea used by **Our Hong Kong Foundation (OHKF)** for about **HK$350 billion** of Hong Kong LAE industry value added by **2050** (September 2025 report). Supporting services are the majority in that projection.

**Why in LAE:** Scale talk needs a clear metric. Value added subtracts intermediate inputs — it is not the same as summing ticket revenue.

**Watch-out:** This is a **think-tank projection**, **not** an HKSAR government number, **not** GDP, **not** your obtainable revenue, and **not** a Mainland 规模 total. Cite [Key figures](key-figures.qmd) / [Official status](tracker.qmd).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="官方中英文本 · Official English and Chinese"}
English: “Based on the latest publicly available data, the industry value added of the LAE in Hong Kong will reach approximately HK\$ 350 billion in 2050, with the majority of value generated in supporting services.” ([source](https://ourhkfoundation.org.hk/en/events/%E3%80%8A%E6%8C%AF%E7%BF%85%E5%95%9F%E8%88%AA-%E2%80%94-%E9%96%8B%E5%89%B5%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E4%BD%8E%E7%A9%BA%E7%B6%93%E6%BF%9F%E6%96%B0%E6%9C%AA%E4%BE%86%E3%80%8B%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E7%99%BC%E5%B8%83%E6%9C%83))

[「根據本報告撰寫時的最新公開數據估算，預計到2050年，本港低空經濟產業的增加價值將達到約3,500億港元，而其中大部分來自配套服務。」]{lang="zh-Hant"} ([source](https://ourhkfoundation.org.hk/tc/events/%E3%80%8A%E6%8C%AF%E7%BF%85%E5%95%9F%E8%88%AA-%E2%80%94-%E9%96%8B%E5%89%B5%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E4%BD%8E%E7%A9%BA%E7%B6%93%E6%BF%9F%E6%96%B0%E6%9C%AA%E4%BE%86%E3%80%8B%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E7%99%BC%E5%B8%83%E6%9C%83))
:::


**[KPI]{#kpi}**  

**What:** **Key performance indicator** — a measurable metric with a clear boundary and owner.

**Why in LAE:** Turns sustainability and equity promises into something you can review and correct.

**Watch-out:** A KPI without a boundary (what counts?) is theatre. See [Week 10](week-10.qmd).

**[LAE]{#lae}**  

**What:** **Low-altitude economy** — economic activity in low-altitude airspace plus the aircraft, sites, digital systems, operators, customers, and supporting services that deliver a **mission**.

**Why in LAE:** The course unit of analysis is a completed service outcome, not only an airframe.

**Watch-out:** Hong Kong’s ~**1,000 m** working description is **policy / economic framing**, **not** a Cap. 448G flying-height limit (ordinary Cap. 448G bands include 100 ft / 300 ft AGL unless CAD permits otherwise). See [What is LAE?](primer.qmd); [Week 1](week-01.qmd); [Key figures](key-figures.qmd).

**[LCA / life-cycle assessment]{#lca}**  

**What:** Assessment of impacts across the full life of a product or service.

**Why in LAE:** “Electric in flight” is not the same as low impact from manufacture to disposal.

**Watch-out:** Do not add GHG Scope 1+2+3 totals to an LCA total without a boundary map. See [Week 10](week-10.qmd).

**[limit pricing]{#limit-pricing}**  

**What:** Pricing or related tactics aimed at deterring entry.

**Why in LAE:** Shared pads and sunk site costs change whether limit pricing is feasible.

**Watch-out:** Classroom stories are not claims about any named Hong Kong operator. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[load factor]{#load-factor}**  

**What:** Traffic carried divided by capacity offered (seats or payload filled ÷ seats or payload available).

**Why in LAE:** Flying often does not help if the aircraft repeatedly flies empty.

**Watch-out:** Load factor is not utilization (how often you fly). You need both. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd) / [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[marginal cost]{#marginal-cost}**  

**What:** Extra cost of one more unit of output (one more flight or passenger, as defined).

**Why in LAE:** Short-run pricing floors and congestion logic start from marginal cost — but ATC still includes fixed cost.

**Watch-out:** Pricing at marginal cost can bankrupt a high-fixed-cost LAE service. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[mode choice]{#mode-choice}**  

**What:** Which travel or delivery option a customer picks (for example MTR vs taxi vs air).

**Why in LAE:** Air wins only if door-to-door generalized cost (and acceptance) beat alternatives.

**Watch-out:** Mode share is an outcome, not an input you may invent. See [Week 4](week-04.qmd).

**[Monte Carlo]{#monte-carlo}**  

**What:** Many random draws from uncertain inputs to show a range of outcomes (and downside risk).

**Why in LAE:** Replaces one heroic base case when demand, weather, and approval timing are uncertain.

**Watch-out:** Concept tool in Week 9 — not a claim that any Hong Kong operator published a Monte Carlo. See [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[network effects]{#network-effects}**  

**What:** Value of a system rises as more users join (or a poor standard can lock everyone in).

**Why in LAE:** Shared information and coordination platforms can tip toward one standard.

**Watch-out:** More nodes raise *possible* links; they do not guarantee demand on each link. See [Week 8](week-08.qmd) / [Week 12](week-12.qmd).

**[NPV / net present value]{#npv}**  

**What:** Whether future cash from a project is worth what you must invest today, after adjusting for timing (and, when stated, risk).

**Why in LAE:** Used as a **screen**: positive NPV under clear assumptions means “might justify investment”; negative means “does not, under those assumptions.”

**Watch-out:** NPV is not a forecast guarantee. A sandbox that cuts delay can improve the *distribution* of NPVs — it does not invent positive margins after partners are paid. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[OEM]{#oem}**  

**What:** **Original equipment manufacturer** — builds the aircraft or key components.

**Why in LAE:** Ticket money is shared along the chain; OEM cost is one slice, not the whole fare.

**Watch-out:** Naming an OEM is not the same as proving Hong Kong certification is done. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[operating profit]{#operating-profit}**  

**What:** Revenue minus operating cost for a period (state what is in or out).

**Why in LAE:** Bridges “customers get value” to “the operator can capture enough to survive.”

**Watch-out:** Define the line items. Partner fees can erase a fat headline fare. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[Pigovian instrument]{#pigovian-instrument}**  

**What:** A tax, charge, or subsidy aimed at an externality.

**Why in LAE:** Classroom peak or noise charges illustrate design ideas for scarce capacity.

**Watch-out:** Hong Kong has **no** drone congestion tax in force as a general rule on this site’s tracker — do not invent one. See [Week 8](week-08.qmd) / [Official status](tracker.qmd).

**[platform / FaaS]{#platform-faas}**  

**What:** Matching or “fly-as-a-service” models, as distinct from owning the fleet.

**Why in LAE:** Asset-light slogans change who holds aircraft risk — they do not remove it.

**Watch-out:** “Asset-light” is not a risk-free business plan. See [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[PPP]{#ppp}**  

**What:** **Public–private partnership** — a long-term deal sharing roles, money, and risk between public and private sides.

**Why in LAE:** Vertiports and public-service missions often need shared investment rules.

**Watch-out:** A PPP does **not** invent demand and is **not** a substitute for a Hong Kong vertiport statute (none dedicated yet). See [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[real options]{#real-options}**  

**What:** The value of flexibility to wait, stage, expand, or exit when uncertainty is high.

**Why in LAE:** Staging a vertiport or fleet beats betting the full CAPEX on day one.

**Watch-out:** Option value needs a real decision gate — not a vague “we might expand.” See [Week 5](week-05.qmd) / [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[revenue management]{#revenue-management}**  

**What:** Allocating scarce capacity and adjusting prices or conditions to improve **expected contribution** — not “fill every seat.”

**Why in LAE:** Empty seats on small aircraft are expensive; mix and fare rules matter.

**Watch-out:** High load factor at a low fare can still miss contribution. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[risk register]{#risk-register}**  

**What:** A table of material risks with a model channel, a response, and a decision trigger / gate.

**Why in LAE:** Capstone and exam answers need risks that change $D$, $K$, cost, or timing — not decoration.

**Watch-out:** A row that never changes the cash-flow path is not a real control. See [Week 11](week-11.qmd).

**[SAM]{#sam}**  

**What:** **Serviceable available market** — the part of the broad market you could realistically serve under stated filters.

**Why in LAE:** Sits between a wide TAM and what capacity can actually serve.

**Watch-out:** SAM is **not** the OHKF HK$350bn figure. See [TAM](#tam); [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[Scope 1 / 2 / 3]{#ghg-scopes}**  

**What:** GHG inventory categories: direct (1), purchased energy (2), and other indirect value-chain (3).

**Why in LAE:** Keeps “electric aircraft” claims honest about whose emissions count.

**Watch-out:** Do not casually add Scopes to an LCA total without boundaries. See [Week 10](week-10.qmd).

**[slot]{#slot}**  

**What:** A right to use scarce pad or airspace capacity at a time.

**Why in LAE:** When pads bind, who flies is an allocation problem (queues, prices, auctions, priority rules).

**Watch-out:** Classroom peak prices are design choices — not a claim about a Hong Kong regulation. See [Week 5](week-05.qmd) / [Week 8](week-08.qmd).

**[Social license]{#social-license}**  

**What:** Ongoing acceptance and trust among affected communities (also written **social licence**).

**Why in LAE:** Legal permission can exist while routes still fail locally on noise or privacy.

**Watch-out:** Traveller choice share is not the same as resident acceptance under the route. See [Week 10](week-10.qmd).

**[sunk cost]{#sunk-cost}**  

**What:** Cost already spent that cannot be recovered.

**Why in LAE:** Entry and pad investment create sunk barriers; limit pricing logic starts here.

**Watch-out:** Sunk cost should not drive “we must keep flying” if forward-looking cash is negative. See [Week 2](week-02.qmd).

**[Supporting services]{#supporting-services}**  

**What:** Finance, insurance, professional services, platforms, and related layers — the segment that accounts for most of OHKF’s 2050 Hong Kong value-added projection.

**Why in LAE:** Hong Kong’s possible role is often framed as a **service layer** beside GBA manufacturing — as a hypothesis to test.

**Watch-out:** OHKF emphasis is not proof of comparative advantage. See [Industry value-added](#industry-value-added).

**[TAM]{#tam}**  

**What:** **Total addressable market** — the broadest relevant set of trips or customers before tight filters.

**Why in LAE:** Useful as a starting funnel step — dangerous as a revenue claim.

**Watch-out:** TAM is **not** OHKF HK$350bn and not obtainable demand. See [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[UAM]{#uam}**  

**What:** **Urban air mobility** — short-distance movement of people or cargo **inside** a dense city; a subset of LAE.

**Why in LAE:** Keeps city passenger/cargo concepts distinct from wider corridor AAM talk.

**Watch-out:** A cargo SUA trial can be LAE without being passenger UAM. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[unconstrained versus constrained market]{#unconstrained-versus-constrained-market}**  

**What:** Theoretical demand versus demand after legal, weather, infrastructure, and acceptance barriers (NASA UAM framing).

**Why in LAE:** Stops unconstrained dollar slides from being pasted into a Hong Kong case.

**Watch-out:** NASA figures are comparators — **not** Hong Kong law or local forecasts. See NASA rows below; [Week 9](week-09.qmd).

**[unit cost]{#unit-cost}**  

**What:** Cost per meaningful unit (per passenger, per flight, per mission-km). Often variable cost plus fixed cost spread over utilization × seats × load factor.

**Why in LAE:** Empty-seat economics: few seats mean fixed cost per passenger explodes unless utilization and load factor are high.

**Watch-out:** State the unit. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd) / [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[usage payment]{#usage-payment}**  

**What:** Payment that rises with actual use (flights, trips, or missions).

**Why in LAE:** Shifts volume risk toward the party that depends on traffic.

**Watch-out:** Usage pay can leave the provider unpaid on grounded days — availability pay is the contrast. See [Week 6](week-06.qmd).

**[utilization]{#utilization}**  

**What:** How intensively an asset is used (for example flights per day).

**Why in LAE:** Higher utilization spreads fixed cost over more flights.

**Watch-out:** Utilization is not load factor. You can fly often with empty seats. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[Value chain]{#value-chain}**  

**What:** Stages from vehicles and sites to operators and supporting services — who creates value and who gets paid.

**Why in LAE:** A high ticket can still leave a thin operator margin after partners are paid.

**Watch-out:** Roles-only maps are not market-share claims. See [How does LAE work?](business-overview.qmd); [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[Value of time]{#value-of-time}**  

**What:** **VOT** — how much a customer is willing to pay to save travel or delivery time.

**Why in LAE:** Turns minutes into money inside generalized cost and fare-ceiling screens.

**Watch-out:** VOT is not demand volume and not NPV by itself. See [Week 1](week-01.qmd).

**[variable cost]{#variable-cost}**  

**What:** Cost that rises with output (for example energy per flight).

**Why in LAE:** Contribution margin = revenue − variable cost; then fixed cost must still be covered.

**Watch-out:** Mis-labeling fixed costs as variable flatters short-run pricing. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[value-added versus 规模 (规模 (Mainland side only))]{#value-added-versus-guimo}**  

**What:** OHKF-style industry **value-added** is not the same metric as Mainland **规模** (scale) totals.

**Why in LAE:** Stops double-counting across borders and metric systems.

**Watch-out:** Do not merge Mainland 低空经济 statistics with Hong Kong OHKF value-added. See [Industry value-added](#industry-value-added); [Official status](tracker.qmd).

**[WTP / willingness to pay]{#wtp}**  

**What:** The most a customer would pay for a service rather than go without.

**Why in LAE:** Starting point for demand curves and fare design — still not a Hong Kong forecast.

**Watch-out:** Individual WTP is not the same as social net benefit or acceptance. See [Week 4](week-04.qmd).

**[yield]{#yield}**  

**What:** Revenue per traffic unit (for example per passenger-km or payload-km).

**Why in LAE:** Pairs with CASK-style cost metrics in unit-economics talk.

**Watch-out:** High yield on tiny volume may not cover fixed cost. See [Week 3](week-03.qmd).

**[NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)]{#nasa}**  
U.S. government agency responsible for science and technology related to air and space; opened **1 Oct 1958**. Course / Readings comparator — **not Hong Kong law**. Institution bio only — do **not** copy UAM market-study unconstrained/constrained dollar figures or TAM from this card; those stay on the separate Course rows below. See also NASA UAM market study constraints; unconstrained versus constrained market; Readings; Timeline. [What Is NASA?](https://www.nasa.gov/learning-resources/for-kids-and-students/what-is-nasa-grades-5-8/); [About](https://www.nasa.gov/about/).

**[NASA UAM market study constraints]{#nasa-uam-market-study-constraints}**  

**What:** In NASA UAM market-study framing, legal, weather, infrastructure, and acceptance barriers shrink an unconstrained market into a constrained one (NASA 2018).

**Why in LAE:** Teaches students not to paste unconstrained dollar / TAM figures into a Hong Kong case.

**Watch-out:** Comparator study only — **not** Hong Kong law and not a local forecast. See also [NASA](#nasa); [unconstrained versus constrained market](#unconstrained-versus-constrained-market).

## Unplaced

- Interoperability / standards
